text:
Talia Benson: Heads up — the internal **Unit Economics dashboard (v1 dogfood)** is now live in Console. 🎉

What it’s for:
• A single finance-aligned view of **blended $/1M output tokens**
• Drilldowns by **model (+ version / quant profile)**, **region**, **customer tier (self-serve / dedicated / private / enterprise)**
• Cost-driver signals: cache hit rate, batching efficiency, avg output length, streaming vs non-streaming

Where:
• Console → Internal → **Unit Economics**
• Direct link: https://console.redwoodinference.com/internal/unit-economics

Who can access:
• Internal-only + feature-flagged. If you get “permission denied”, drop a note here w/ your email + team and we’ll add you.

Dogfood ask (please do this week):
1) Pick a time range (last 7d is fine) + your most used model
2) Check that trends + top-N tables “make sense”
3) Try at least one drilldown path (e.g., Model → Region, or Tier → Model)

How to give feedback:
• Reply in this thread w/:
  - link to the view (copy URL with filters)
  - what you expected vs what you saw
  - screenshot if UI/formatting
  - if it feels like a data issue: include the model/region/tier + time window
• Bugs: file under **ENG → “Unit Econ Dashboard”** component (or just @ me and I’ll triage)

Known limitations (v1 dogfood):
• Some views may show a “low confidence” indicator if coverage is incomplete (e.g., missing tier/region tagging)
• Reconciliation report vs billing totals exists but still being tuned (Finance signoff in progress)
• Streaming token parity is improved vs last week, but please flag anything suspicious

Owners on standby: @Felix Schneider (API), @Nora Ahmed (UI), @Mei Lin (warehouse/views), @Caleb Johnson (data quality), @Allison Grant/@Sean Gallagher (alerts/SLOs)

Thanks in advance — this is the measurement foundation for batching/caching/quant cost work, so real usage feedback is super helpful.

Marissa Cole: :raised_hands: If you’re in Product / Optimize land, would love feedback on whether the default view + filters are the right “starting point” for investigations. We can tweak defaults before Finance starts using this for weekly readouts.

Felix Schneider: FYI query caching is on (short TTL). If you’re hammering filters and see slightly stale numbers for a minute, that’s expected. If anything looks >1h stale, please call it out.

Allison Grant: Also if you see the “data freshness” banner, please screenshot + paste in thread. We’re validating alert thresholds and would rather get false positives now than later.

Dylan Brooks: +1 please be ruthless about confusing labeling (blended vs marginal). If the page makes you ask “wait what exactly is included?” that’s a bug.

Laura Bennett: Thanks. For dogfood: can we pin a standard time range for Finance folks to test (e.g., QTD) or do you prefer last 7d for now?

Talia Benson: Good call — for now please do **last 7d** first (less backfill variance). We’ll do a separate Finance-only pass on **QTD** once the reconciliation view is green.

Rishi Malhotra: When you say “blended” here, is this the version that includes idle capacity allocation for Dedicated pools?

Mei Lin: Yes — blended includes allocated idle per ADR. Dedicated pools allocate idle within the pool (not across hosted). There’s a tooltip in the metric definition, but we should probably make that more obvious.

Nora Ahmed: If anyone hits weird filter behavior (esp. tier + region combos), pls paste the URL. There’s a known edge case w/ resetting the secondary breakdown when switching the primary group-by.

Sean Gallagher: Re: access — don’t post screenshots with any customer-identifying info. Top-Ns should be aggregated + redacted, but if you see anything that looks like a customer id/name, flag immediately.

Caleb Johnson: Data quality note: if you see a sudden dip to near-zero tokens for a segment, check the “coverage” bar in the footer — that’s usually a missing dimension emission vs real traffic drop. Still worth reporting.

Talia Benson: ^ +1 and please keep feedback in this thread for now so we can centralize. We’ll open a dedicated channel once we’re past initial triage.

Marissa Cole: Example feedback format that’s super helpful:
• View link: <url>
• Issue: “eu-west looks 2x cost vs us-east for same model, started Feb 2”
• Expected: “within ~10–20% given rate card”
• Notes: “mostly streaming, average output length ~800”

Talia Benson: Thanks all — keep it coming. We’ll post a quick status update end of week with top issues + what’s fixed.
